sections.html:
Camas is a Clark County city on the Columbia River, about 20 miles northeast of Portland, with Vancouver on its west side and Washougal on its east. The city counts 27,749 residents as of July 1, 2025, a 6.0 percent rise over the April 2020 base. Nearly four of five homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $711,700. Households average close to three people. Buyers are typically families, so bedrooms, yards and school boundaries get close attention. County-level steps run through Clark County offices.

sections.h2: Layout, schools and the mill site
sections.html:
Lakes, creeks and Prune Hill shape what buyers see. Prune Hill, an extinct volcanic vent, rises in the middle of town, and Lacamas Lake, Round Lake, Lacamas Creek, the Washougal River and the Columbia River all lie inside city limits. Lacamas Park runs along State Route 500 with trails around the lakes.

  • Downtown Camas: the historic core near the paper mill, with the Liberty Theatre and the festival calendar, including Camas Days.
  • Prune Hill: a hillside residential area with a sports park named for it.
  • Lacamas Lake and Round Lake: lakeside homes next to park trails and boat launches.
  • Grass Valley and Forest Home: areas with city parks of the same names.

The Camas School District covers most of town. Some small areas belong to Evergreen Public Schools, which is worth checking for any listing address. Demolition of the paper mill has proceeded, with work expected to finish by 2027, and the site is expected to become waterfront on Camas Slough as an extension of downtown. Buyers who ask about the neighborhood's direction will likely ask about that project.

Camas adopted Ordinance 25-025 in 2025 to align with new state housing rules. The city's ADU definition is a unit of up to 1,000 square feet, attached, detached or a mix of the two, and each lot may hold up to two. Camas also allows two middle housing units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable, and it created a unit lot subdivision process that lets parent lots divide into separately owned child lots.

These rules can add value, and they create questions for sellers. ADUs count toward the middle housing total, so a lot with one main home can add two ADUs, while a lot that already holds two middle housing units cannot. Before you list, confirm what was permitted.

  • Ask the Camas Community Development Department, which has Planning, Development Engineering and Building divisions, for permit history on garage conversions, basements and additions.
  • Applications, inspection requests and status tracking all go through the city's online permit system, live since June 12, 2024.

Most Camas listings are polished and move-in ready, which makes a house needing work easy to spot. A seller in a hurry usually weighs three paths:

  • Prepare and list: fix, stage and show for a few weeks. This brings the best price for a home in good condition.
  • Sell as-is to an investor or cash buyer: a fit for postponed maintenance, an estate, an empty house or a tenant problem, and you choose the closing date.
  • Negotiate a leaseback or delayed possession: helpful when you need time to move after closing.

Request proof of funds and a clear written offer from any buyer. Then compare net proceeds, not only price: excise tax, payoff of any loan and prorated property taxes all come off the top.

A deeded transfer sends three items to the treasurer in the property's county, the Clark County Treasurer for Camas: the affidavit, the deed and the payment. Claim only one exemption per transfer, and hold your records for at least four years. Overpaid? Ask for a refund within four years of the sale.

State excise tax climbs by tier. Price up to $525,000 pays 1.1 percent, the slice from there to $1,525,000 pays 1.28 percent, and higher tiers follow. Your escrow officer can price the local add-on and the exact bill.

You also owe the buyer a seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020, normally within five business days of mutual acceptance. The form covers title, water, sewer, structural and other topics, and you sign and date each page. Camas houses near lakes, creeks or slopes should have drainage and septic or sewer details ready, since those questions appear on the form.

Clark County splits real property tax into April 30 and October 31 installments. Statements for the first half are ready by March 15, and second-half statements typically by September 15. Once October 31 passes, the following installment is due the next April 30.

From 2023 onward, a late residential parcel of four or fewer units owes 0.75 percent interest per month and no penalty. A mailed payment counts only with a postmark on or before the due date. The county does not take prepayment of future-year taxes now, apart from certain sale transactions such as personal property and mobile homes. Call 564.397.2252 or email treasoff@clark.wa.gov, and ask about the county's tax relief programs for homeowners who meet eligibility requirements.

Camas buyers are mostly families, and they ask practical questions. Have the permit history for any garage conversion, basement or addition, and know whether an ADU exists and what was approved. If the house sits near Lacamas Lake, Round Lake, a creek or a slope, collect drainage and septic or sewer details. Bring your latest Clark County tax statement and a plan for the school district answer. The city's Community Development Department and the county treasurer are the two offices to call.

Once you accept an offer, escrow opens and title work shows any unpaid taxes. You sign the disclosure form, deed and affidavit, and payment goes to the Clark County Treasurer. Escrow prorates property taxes and deducts any loan payoff from what you receive. No lender means no appraisal, and a house that needs work can still close on a date you pick. Gather your tax statement, permit history and the disclosure form ahead of time so nothing holds up the signing, and ask the treasurer about any balance before the closing date.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Camas homes?
faqs.a: The Camas School District covers most of the city, but a few small areas are in Evergreen Public Schools. Confirm the district for the exact address.

faqs.q: How many ADUs can I build on a Camas lot?
faqs.a: Up to two. Camas defines an ADU as a unit up to 1,000 square feet, attached or detached. ADUs count toward the middle housing allowance, which is two units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half or the full year, October 31 for the second. A mailed payment must be postmarked by the due date. Late residential tax on four or fewer units accrues 0.75 percent per month.

faqs.q: Who collects the excise tax on a Camas home sale?
faqs.a: The Clark County Treasurer, because that is the county where Camas properties sit. The seller usually pays, and a deeded transfer sends the affidavit, deed and payment together.

faqs.q: Do I need to keep records of an excise tax exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, for at least four years. You can claim only one exemption per transfer, and any overpayment refund request is due within four years of the sale.
